title: Paying for It
objective: After this level you can explain how taxes fund government.
summary: Taxes are compulsory, unrequited payments on what people earn, buy and own. In 2024 they averaged 34.1% of GDP across OECD countries, from 18.3% in Mexico to 45.2% in Denmark.

cards.headline: A bus fare buys you a ride. What does a tax buy you?
cards.body: You hand over money either way. But the two deals work in completely different ways, and that difference is what makes a tax a tax.

cards.headline: Compulsory and unrequited
cards.body: The OECD defines taxes as compulsory, unrequited payments to government. Compulsory: you can't opt out. Unrequited: what you get back from government isn't in proportion to what you paid. A fare buys one ride. Your taxes buy nothing in particular, and help pay for Level 5's whole list.

items.label: What you earn
points: Social security contributions and payroll taxes on wages

cards.fact: Across OECD countries, taxes come to about a third of GDP.
cards.context: GDP measures the value of everything a country produces in a year. In 2024, taxes averaged 34.1% of GDP across OECD countries, per the OECD's Revenue Statistics 2025. The range was wide: 18.3% in Mexico, 45.2% in Denmark. How big that share should be is a political choice, and countries make it very differently.

mascot.line: Same idea, very different sizes. Why anyone should agree to pay at all is Level 7's question.

cards.headline: Taxes: explained
learned: Taxes are compulsory and unrequited payments
They fall on what you earn, buy and own
From 18.3% in Mexico to 45.2% in Denmark

questions.prompt: In the OECD's definition, what does it mean that a tax is "unrequited"?

options.label: You can choose whether to pay it
options.rationale: That's the opposite of how taxes work.

options.label: It is paid only once in your life
options.rationale: Taxes are paid again and again.

options.label: What you get back isn't in proportion to what you paid
It must be spent on the thing that was taxed
options.rationale: Tax money isn't tied to what was taxed.

questions.explanation: Unrequited means the benefits government provides aren't normally in proportion to what each person pays.

questions.prompt: In 2024, taxes across OECD countries averaged about what share of GDP?

options.label: About a tenth
options.rationale: Even Mexico, the lowest, was near a fifth.

options.label: About a half
options.rationale: Even Denmark, the highest, was below a half.

options.label: About nine-tenths
options.rationale: Far too high; the average was 34.1%.

questions.explanation: The 2024 average was 34.1% of GDP, from 18.3% in Mexico to 45.2% in Denmark.

questions.prompt: Level 5's free riders enjoy public goods without paying. Which feature of taxes stops them?

options.label: Taxes are only on property
options.rationale: Taxes fall on earnings, spending and property.

options.label: Taxes are set by each person
options.rationale: Nobody sets their own tax; that would invite free riding.

options.label: Taxes buy one specific service
options.rationale: Taxes are unrequited: they don't buy a specific service.

questions.explanation: Because taxes are compulsory, everyone contributes, so nobody can free ride on public goods.
